title: 2001 AMC 12 Problem 18
statement: A circle centered at \(A\) with a radius of \(1\) and a circle centered at \(B\) with a radius of \(4\) are externally tangent. A third circle is tangent to the first two and to one of their common external tangents as shown. The radius of the third circle is

solutions.text:
When two mutually tangent circles of radii \(r\) and \(s\) both rest on a line, the distance between their points of tangency is \(2\sqrt{rs}.\)

The big circles’ contact points are \(2\sqrt{1 \cdot 4} = 4\) apart. Placing the small circle of radius \(x\) between them, its two tangent distances add up: \[ 2\sqrt{1 \cdot x} + 2\sqrt{4 \cdot x} = 4. \]

Then \(6\sqrt{x} = 4,\) so \(\sqrt{x} = \dfrac{2}{3}\) and \(x = \dfrac{4}{9}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: For two circles of radii \(r\) and \(s\) both tangent to a line and to each other, their contact points on the line are \(2\sqrt{rs}\) apart
The contact point of the small circle splits the segment: \(2\sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{4x} = 2\sqrt{4}\)
